articleTitle: Research on Ad Hoc network Coverage Optimization for Unmanned Aerial Vehicles based on improved Zebra Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of low network coverage due to uneven node deployment in UAV ad hoc networks, the multi-strategy improved Zebra Optimization Algorithm Network Coverage (MZOC) is proposed for UAV ad hoc networks to improve the shortcomings of insufficient optimization accuracy and easy-to-fall into local optimum. Firstly, the Circle chaotic mapping is introduced in the initial phase to generate chaotic sequences to obtain a more uniform search space; secondly, the nonlinear weights and golden sine strategy are introduced in the foraging phase to optimize and update the zebra positions in the foraging phase; and lastly, the adaptive t-distribution perturbation strategy is introduced in the defense phase to improve the algorithm’s performance of searching for the optimum. A comparison of simulation experiments shows that the coverage rate of the MZOC algorithm proposed in this paper is ${3. 3 5 3} \%, {1 5. 2 3 7 \%}$, and ${3. 1 3 7 \%}$ higher than that of the ZOA, EO algorithm, and GWO algorithm, respectively, which improves the phenomenon of uneven distribution of the nodes and improves the utilization rate of the nodes.

articleTitle: Research on database splitting methodology for microservicization of monolithic applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This study introduces the BLDD method for database disassembly, enhancing automation in migrating monolithic applications to microservices by integrating service and database separation. It refines software analysis tools to automatically gather class and database access data, then applies a multiobjective genetic algorithm to optimize service splitting. Experimental results demonstrate that BLDD offers architects a more objective and automated approach, simplifying the migration process.

articleTitle: Adaptive Deep Learning Algorithm for Vulnerability Detection and Repair in Big Data Audit System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To solve the problems of low detection accuracy and delayed repair response in complex situations such as massive data streams, frequent changes, and diverse attack methods faced by big data auditing, this project plans to adopt adaptive deep learning (DL) technology to dynamically optimize the detection and repair process, improve the security performance of the system, and meet the rapidly changing data environment. Firstly, this project plans to use a combination of multi-layer convolutional neural networks (CNN) and long short-term memory networks (LSTM) for in-depth research. Secondly, a learning method based on adaptive learning is proposed, which enables dynamic adjustment of the established model according to changes in the environment in different application scenarios. On this basis, a maintenance decision optimization method based on deep reinforcement learning is proposed. The accuracy of this algorithm remains at a level of $0.928-0.933$ as the complexity of the scene increases. The response time for the correction will be slightly extended, from 1.9 ms to 2.3 ms, due to the increased complexity of the scenario. Through testing of the BD system, the effectiveness of this method has been verified, providing a new perspective for the security issues of the BD system.

articleTitle: Radar Artificial Modulation Signal Recognition Based on Multi-Source Feature Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The recognition of radar artificial modulated signals, achieved through comprehensive analysis and precise identification of the modulation characteristics inherent to radar signals, holds critical importance for differentiating enemy radar emissions and enhancing the anti-jamming capabilities of radar systems. Nevertheless, current recognition methodologies, including support vector machines and long short-term memory network (LSTM) networks, exhibit certain limitations in terms of accuracy. To address this issue, we propose a multi-source feature fusion (MSFF) network aimed at augmenting the recognition performance of artificially modulated radar signals. This network employs short-time Fourier transform (STFT) techniques to process the artificially modulated radar signal and utilizes phase spectrum, real part, and imaginary part as input features to effectively extract essential signal characteristics, thereby significantly improving recognition accuracy. Simulation experiments demonstrate that this network achieves a remarkable recognition accuracy of 99.15%, showcasing its superior effectiveness compared to six typical neural networks.

articleTitle: DWT-Net: A Medical Image Segmentation Model Incorporating Frequency Domain Information
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Numerous medical image segmentation frameworks have been proposed by researchers; however, the incorporation of frequency domain information has been largely overlooked in previous studies. By incorporating frequency information, we avoid the issue where traditional downsampling reduces computational load and communication bandwidth but also removes redundant and important information, leading to accuracy loss. This paper introduces a novel supervised convolutional neural network architecture, termed “DWT-Net,” which incorporates discrete wavelet convolution and a custom residual downsampling mechanism. Through wavelet transformation, the model not only achieves a near-global receptive field but also significantly enhances its responsiveness to low-frequency information. To bolster the model’s performance, data augmentation techniques were employed to enrich the dataset. Our model has been applied to the public datasets Kvasir-SEG and CVCClinicDB. Compared to other frameworks, it has shown significant improvements in display, achieving the state-of-the-art accuracy.

articleTitle: DDoS Attack Detection Method Based on Improved Bagging
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In view of the complexity and concealment of distributed denial of service attacks, a DDoS attack detection method based on improved Bagging ensemble learning is proposed. In order to effectively deal with the changing attack modes and improve the stability and accuracy of the detection model, this method enhances the recognition ability of DDoS attacks by introducing a weighted voting mechanism and combining multiple machine learning algorithms. Experiments on the CIC-DDoS2019 dataset show that after preprocessing steps such as feature selection, data normalization and feature correlation analysis, the improved Bagging model using RF, DT and KNN as base learners has an accuracy of $\mathbf{9 9. 9 8 \%}$ on the test set, which is significantly better than the traditional Bagging method and other detection models. This study shows that the improved Bagging method not only improves the accuracy and robustness of DDoS attack detection, but also provides new ideas for solving challenges such as high-dimensional data processing and dynamic network traffic analysis.

articleTitle: A Deep Network based on Dual Attention for Oracle Bone Inscription Character Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Oracle bone inscriptions, as the earliest systematic written records in China, are invaluable for understanding ancient history and the evolution of writing. However, their diverse forms, irregular shapes, and ambiguous carvings pose significant challenges for recognition. To address these issues, we propose a Dual Attention Network (DANet) for oracle bone character recognition. DANet introduces a Dual Attention Module (DAM) consisting of Position Attention and Channel Attention, which effectively capture position and channel features to improve recognition accuracy. Experiments on the two public datasets HWOBC and OBC306 demonstrate that our proposed method achieves superior performance compared to classical deep learning models. The results show improvements in both Top-1 Accuracy and Top-5 Accuracy, confirming the effectiveness of the proposed framework.

articleTitle: LiteYOLOv8: A Lightweight Model for Real-Time Object Detection in Remote Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: As the demand for object detection in remote sensing imagery increases, achieving model lightweighting without sacrificing detection accuracy has become a critical challenge in current research. The YOLO series of convolutional models, known for their high inference speed and accuracy, are widely employed in object detection tasks. Existing optimization techniques, such as Partial Convolution (PConv) and Depthwise Convolution (DWConv), are effective in reducing model parameters and Floating Point Operations (FLOPs), but they often lead to a decline in detection accuracy. To address this, we propose LiteYOLOv8, a lightweight object detection model based on YOLOv8. The model introduces a novel SPC2 module in the Backbone and Neck feature extraction stages, leveraging PConv for lightweight design and enhancing feature extraction through Channel Shuffle. In the Detection Head, DWConv is employed for lightweight classification and regression, while PConv is incorporated to resolve the limitations in cross-channel information interaction. Experimental results demonstrate that LiteYOLOv8 achieves detection accuracy comparable to the original YOLOv8 model on the SSDD, Sar-Aircraftv1.0, and FAIR1M datasets, while it reduces the parameter count by $\mathbf{4 1. 7 \%}$ and the FLOPs by $\mathbf{4 6. 9 \%}$.

articleTitle: A Fast and Robust SAR-Optical Image Registration Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In recent years, the rapid advancement of remote sensing technology has led to significant progress in the field of heterogeneous remote sensing image registration. However, most existing heterogeneous image registration algorithms primarily rely on structural features, gradient information, or phase consistency of the images for registration. This approach poses significant challenges in terms of registration accuracy and efficiency when dealing with remote sensing images of nonuniform texture scenes, such as areas containing oceans, deserts, and forests. To address these issues, this paper proposes a fast and robust image registration algorithm tailored for non-uniform texture regions. The algorithm first employs an adaptive regionaware feature point extraction method to distinguish between effective and weak texture regions, thereby enhancing the registration robustness for scenes with significant regional differences. Secondly, it utilizes a single-scale orientated gradient fusion operator to construct feature descriptors, which not only allows for the rapid construction of feature descriptions but also boasts high accuracy. Finally, accurate image registration is achieved through fast template matching in the frequency domain based on non-maximum suppression. The application of this algorithm to the registration task of heterogeneous images with non-uniform texture regions demonstrates significant improvements in both registration accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: Research on Signaling Security Analysis of 5G Core Roaming Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: As a pioneering form of mobile communication technology, the 5 G core (5 GC) network roaming function is of paramount importance in ensuring the optimal utilization of network resources and preventing the unnecessary replication of infrastructure. However, as 5GC network roaming is being promoted commercially, the issue of signaling security is becoming increasingly prominent. This paper presents an analysis of the network architecture, inter-network interfaces, and roaming routing mechanism of 5GC network roaming, with a particular focus on the potential network signaling security risks associated with the Security Edge Protection Proxy (SEPP) and (hNRF) for 5GC network roaming. Such incidents include the leakage of sensitive information and the occurrence of signaling fraud. Furthermore, it is recommended that the combined Category 1 (CAT1), Category 2 (CAT2), and Category 3 (CAT3) be used for messages of different services, different interfaces, different service types, and different operations in the 5GC network in order to migrate risks and enhance the resilience of the communication network security.

articleTitle: Differentially private data synthesis method based on nonlinear mapping embedding
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a synthetic data generation method Privnpgd based on private-PGD. private-PGD is a differential data generation method that utilizes optimal transmission and particle gradient descent to effectively fit the probability distribution of noisy data. It is superior to other synthetic data models in handling large data sets. Our research focuses on the embedding phase and particle gradient descent phase of attribute fields, where the percentiles of attribute fields are calculated and the discrete properties are mapped to these percentiles using nonlinear functions, and the stability and convergence of particle renewal are improved using energy function-based slice distributions. This method effectively captures the non-uniform distribution of data while preserving the sequence information of discrete attributes. It generates synthetic data on some discretized datasets and outperforms both private-pgd and existing methods.

articleTitle: Prediction of Imaging Quality based on Hybrid Quantum-Classical Neural Network Model
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Optical imaging systems are widely used in daily life. Due to long-term exposure to the environment, the life of the camera will be affected. This paper analyzes the gray scale value change of the imaging quality of the optical imaging system during the gas corrosion process, and uses the gray scale value to define the pictures taken by the camera after aging. Learning the imaging quality of the camera through the hybrid quantum-classical neural network model can predict the imaging quality of the optical system well and give early warning to the aging system.

articleTitle: Multi-population artificial bee colony algorithm based on Lagrange interpolation
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The artificial bee colony (ABC) algorithm, inspired by bees’ foraging, solves optimization problems well but converges slowly due to its search equation’s bias towards exploration. This paper proposes the MPABCLI based on Lagrange interpolation. It divides individuals into sub-populations by fitness, uses different variation strategies, limits candidate parents’ range, and adds Lagrangian interpolation local search (LSLI) to balance exploration and exploitation. Tests on CEC2014’s 30 functions show that for 10D, 30D and 50D problems, MPABCLI outperforms other ABC algorithms, with better performance and accuracy for global numerical optimization.

articleTitle: Multi-Pedestrian Tracking by Decoupling Confidence Weighting and Hierarchical Appearance Embedding Updates
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The advent of powerful object detectors has led to the widespread adoption of the “tracking-by-detection” paradigm in multi-object tracking (MOT). However, challenges such as association errors during occlusions continue to hinder tracking performance. To address this issue, we propose three key improvements. First, we leverage the confidence scores generated by a detector with decoupled heads to weight the cost matrix. Second, we introduce a height-constrained intersection-over-union (IoU) distance metric. Finally, we classify the appearance features of objects in the current frame into two levels—high and low—based on their respective confidence scores. These features are then matched and updated against stored appearance embeddings from previous frames. Extensive comparative and ablation experiments conducted on the MOT17 dataset demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves tracking performance in multi-object tracking scenarios.

articleTitle: Line Fault Detection Strategy for Multi-Microcontroller Systems Based on PSO-GA Optimized SVM
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an innovative real-time fault detection method for multi-monolithic computer (MCU) systems that combines a lightweight interpretable artificial intelligence (XAI)-enhanced support vector machine (SVM) and an improved hybrid particle swarm optimization (PSO)-genetic algorithm (GA) optimization technique. XAI-SVM achieves efficient and interpretable fault detection by integrating the high accuracy of a traditional SVM with the XAI-SVM achieves efficient and interpretable fault detection by combining the high accuracy of traditional SVM with the interpretability of Shapley Additive Properties (SHAP), while optimized for resource constrained MCU environments. The improved PSO-GA hybrid optimization algorithm effectively balances global exploration and local exploitation by introducing an adaptive weighting mechanism, which significantly improves the optimization efficiency of XAI-SVM hyperparameters. In addition, a distributed fault detection framework is developed in this paper, which improves the reliability and robustness of the overall system by coordinating multiple MCUs and introducing a lightweight consensus mechanism. Test results show that compared with existing methods, the method proposed in this paper achieves higher fault detection accuracy and interpretability in a multi-MCU system while maintaining excellent real-time performance. The method shows significant improvement in detection efficiency, result interpretability and system adaptability, and is particularly suitable for complex industrial application scenarios requiring fast and accurate fault identification and diagnosis.

articleTitle: Research and Construction of Multi-model Fusionbased Malicious URL Detection Method
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: While the rapid development of the Internet brings convenience to people’s lives, it also breeds network security threats that use malicious URL (Uniform Resource Locator) as an entry point, such as phishing attacks and malware distribution. These attacks may lead to data leakage, system damage, and financial loss, therefore, effective detection and blocking of malicious URLs are crucial for network security. In this paper, we compare the performance of several mainstream supervised learning methods for malicious URL detection and construct a two-layer stacked integration model that combines random forests, extreme trees, and XGBoost as base models, and decision trees as metamodels. The experimental results show that the model in this study achieves 0.92 accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score under cross-validation with an AUC value of 0.95, The experimental results show that the model performs well in terms of accuracy, balance, and robustness. This multi-model fusion method not only improves the detection accuracy but also enhances the system’s ability to process large-scale data, which provides strong support for building an efficient and reliable malicious URL detection system.

articleTitle: A novel block-based Interpolation reversible data hiding algorithm using dual image
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Reversible Data Hiding(RDH) algorithm is to embed as much secret data as possible in a reversible manner while maintaining image quality. We propose a dual-image, block-based interpolation algorithm, eliminating down-sampling and ensuring full recovery of the cover image with improved watermarked image quality. Firstly, duplicate the cover image into two dual images. Then, the dual images are divided into $2 \times 2$ non-overlapping blocks, embed the secret data into different non-reference pixels of the two dual images using an interpolation algorithm. We demonstrate that the secret data can be correctly extracted, the cover image is fully recovered, and there are no overflow or underflow problems. Experiments results showed our algorithm makes progress in both embedding capacity, image quality and can stand some steganographic analysis.

articleTitle: A Second-order Sallen-Key Low-pass Filter with Switched Capacitors
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper presents a second-order Sallen-Key low-pass filter structure that uses switch capacitors (SC) as equivalent substitutes for resistors. Two non-overlapping clocks can be generated through an external clock circuit, which can then control the MOS switch state and effectively replace the resistors in the filter, thereby achieving the goal of saving silicon chip area, improving integration, and optimizing circuit accuracy.

articleTitle: Research on Multi-Channel Phase Control Technology for Inter-Satellite Laser Communication
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To solve the problem that it is difficult to achieve consistent phases in fiber channels in the inter-satellite laser communication system and ensure that the image fields of each sub-aperture can form the principal maximum at the center of the Airy disk under far-field interference, thus obtaining high-quality communication signals, this paper focuses on the homodyne interference phase control technology based on preprocessing algorithms. Firstly, a dual-channel phase error model is established in this paper, the influencing factors of phase detection accuracy are analyzed, and a new preprocessing phase calculation method is proposed. To verify the feasibility of the phase detection algorithm, a dual-channel phase control experimental system is constructed. The experimental results show that under the condition of a camera frame rate of 290 Hz, the closed-loop control bandwidth of the system reaches 285 Hz, and the phase control accuracy is $\lambda / 30$, The phase control accuracy meets the requirements of the inter-satellite laser communication system, and the system can work stably for a long period of time. The experiments also prove that under the condition of $640 \times 512$ full-frame sampling, the phase control of hundreds or even thousands of channel arrays can be achieved, which provides important technical support for the application of multi-element channels in the inter-satellite laser communication system.

articleTitle: Research on Pedestrian Detection Algorithm Based on Improved YOLOv5s
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To address the issues of insufficient detection accuracy and an excessive number of model parameters under small targets and occlusion conditions in the pedestrian recognition task, the present study develops a modified YOLOv5s model specifically tailored for detecting pedestrians. Through the replacement of the convolutional layers of YOLOv5s with the lighter Ghost module, the computational volume is reduced and the feature extraction is accelerated; Simultaneously, by adopting the CBAM attention mechanism in the Neck’s feature fusion layer, we significantly improve the performance of network learning ability and improves the detection accuracy; and the SIoU Loss function is adopted in YOLOv5s, which further accelerates the training speed and improve the detection frame localization accuracy. Through this paper comparative experiment, the improved YOLOv5s on the optimized WiderPerson dataset achieves a 5.3% increase in $A P$, achieves a reduction of 2.21 M in the model’s parameter size and reduces the GFLOPs by 46.2%.

articleTitle: Jitter Analysis and Decomposition Based on Tail-Fit Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Jitter is one of the main reasons that affect the quality of high-speed serial signal transmission. The jitter value is analyzed quickly and accurately in order to take corresponding measures to reduce jitter and improve signal quality. In this paper, the Tail-Fit algorithm is compared with the jitter decomposition based on spectral analysis, and the feasibility of Tail-Fit algorithm is verified by simulation. Compared with the jitter decomposition algorithm based on spectral analysis, TailFit algorithm has shorter operation time, lower complexity, lower requirements for input signal, and higher accuracy when deterministic jitter is much larger than random jitter.

articleTitle: Security Control Techniques for Device Access in 5G-enabled Manufacturing Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper explores integrating 5G technology into manufacturing to enhance intelligent perception, precise control, and communication, leveraging its wide coverage, high capacity, speed, and low latency to advance digitalisation, increase production, and reduce costs. However, the deployment of 5G in settings faces challenges such as over-reliance on wired connections and stringent data security requirements. To address these issues, we propose a comprehensive system architecture incorporating an indoor coverage system with small 5G base stations and secure access methods for typical devices. Additionally, we introduce two key technologies to enhance device security: a specialised protection technique for 5G application devices and a trusted access security control technology. These solutions aim to improve the security, reliability, and stability of 5G-enabled manufacturing, thereby meeting the sector’s high standards for performance, security and confidentiality.

articleTitle: Dual-Mode Broadband GaN HEMT Power Amplifier for Continuous Wave and Pulse Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To address the integration requirements of next-generation electronic equipment, this study presents a dual-mode power amplifier capable of switching between continuous wave/pulse mode by adjusting the operating voltage. The output impedance of the power amplifier varies under different bias voltages. This paper proposes a gallium nitride high electron mobility transistor (GaN HEMT) dual-mode power amplifier, which achieves broadband, high-power matching at both voltages by examining the output impedance characteristics of the power transistor core across varying voltages and optimizing within the impedance domain. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed power amplifier delivers an output power exceeding 53 dBm in 48 V pulse mode with a typical drain efficiency of $\mathbf{4 2 \%}$, and achieves over 50 dBm in 28 V CW mode with a typical drain efficiency of 40%

articleTitle: Long-term network traffic prediction based on learnable trend seasonal decomposition
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The continuous growth of network traffic has introduced increasingly complex challenges in network management. Accurate forecasting of future network traffic is essential for optimizing network utilization. Mobile operators can leverage long-term network traffic forecasts to optimize network planning and resource allocation, thereby enhancing the quality of service provided to users. Current network traffic prediction methods either utilize moving average (MA) techniques to decompose input network traffic into trends or employ learnable network layers to achieve decomposition into trend and seasonal components. However, the selection of convolution kernels in these methods often necessitates extensive experimentation, making the prediction performance highly dependent on prior knowledge. To overcome these limitations, we propose a neural network model incorporating learnable trend-seasonal decomposition for longterm mobile network traffic prediction. To achieve time series decomposition, we replace the single fixed convolution kernel with multiple learnable convolutional layers. Furthermore, we adopt a down-convolution-up-convolution network architecture to effectively extract the traffic trends, minimizing information loss during the convolution process. In the experiments, we evaluated the predictive performance of the proposed model in comparison with the current state-of-theart models. The experimental results demonstrate that, compared to various existing TSP(Time Series Forecasting) prediction models, the proposed model achieves superior accuracy in longterm mobile network traffic forecasting, underscoring its potential for effective application in long-term traffic analysis.

articleTitle: Research on Distance Measurement Methods for Standing Long Jump
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: With the increasing focus on physical exercise, the standing long jump has become a significant measure of adolescents’ physical fitness. Traditional distance measurement methods for standing long jumps are either subjective, cumbersome, or lack precision. This study introduces a standardized, computer vision-based approach that automates the measurement process, enabling simultaneous testing and interference resistance. By employing object detection, keypoint detection, and key pose classification models, our method ensures high-precision distance measurement without the need for test subjects to wear electronic devices. The aim of this research is to enhance the accuracy and efficiency of standing long jump assessments, providing a reliable tool for physical fitness evaluations.

articleTitle: A Study on Multi-Class Laryngoscope Image Semantic Segmentation Using Attention U-Net and a Composite Loss
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Laryngoscopy is an important clinical diagnostic tool in otolaryngology. Precisely segmenting multiple types of structures in laryngoscopic images can aid physicians in making informed decisions. However, traditional U-Net models struggle with complex multi-class structures and class imbalance in such images. We propose a multi-class semantic segmentation approach based on the Attention U-Net architecture, trained with a composite loss function that combines cross-entropy and a multi-class Dice loss. Experimental results show that compared to conventional U-Net, the proposed method significantly improves multi-class segmentation accuracy and generalization.

articleTitle: Construction of Local Height Maps Based on Spherical Coordinates
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Point cloud denoising is crucial for 3D point clouds. This paper improves a multi-patch collaborative denoising method based on local frames, adopting a spherical coordinate method on the basis of the original rectangular coordinate system established for local frames. In the original local frames, this method performs spherical fitting for local neighborhood points, then projects the neighborhood points onto the sphere, with the position on the sphere serving as the height map’s position coordinates, and the distance from the sphere as the height map’s height coordinates.

articleTitle: SPATH: A Transformer Spatiotemporal Prediction Framework with GAT-based Hierarchical Fusion Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Effective temporal-spatial sequence prediction remains challenging due to the complex interactions between temporal patterns and spatial dependencies. Traditional approaches and recent Transformer-based models often struggle to capture these intricate relationships, either processing temporal and spatial features separately or using simple fusion mechanisms. To address these challenges, we propose a novel prediction framework based on GAT-enhanced Hierarchical Fusion Network (HFN). Our framework introduces three key innovations: (1) a hierarchical fusion architecture that progressively integrates temporal and spatial information through cross-attention and graph attention networks, (2) a novel aspect-based attention mechanism that dynamically weights feature dimensions based on their semantic importance, and (3) an optimized encoder-decoder structure that efficiently processes long sequences while maintaining prediction accuracy. Experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that our framework consistently outperforms advanced Transformer variants including Reformer, Informer, and STTN, achieving significant performance improvements. The results validate the effectiveness of our hierarchical fusion approach in capturing complex temporal-spatial dependencies.

articleTitle: System design of a class-D audio power amplifier circuit with high-precision AGC control
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Aiming at the problem of poor human auditory sensation caused by the wide range variation of audio signal amplitude, a high-precision and expandable automatic volume control circuit system is designed, which combines the software AGC circuit with the hardware AGC circuit, and is verified in the circuit system composed of MSPM0G3507 microcontroller and VCA810. The circuit system realizes high-precision, fast, and high-energy-ratio volume control through the adjustment of algorithms and circuit parameters, and at the same time has a certain degree of expandability and operability due to the presence of the microcontroller.

articleTitle: A Filtering Rat-Race Coupler Based on Coupling-Enhanced Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper proposed a filtering Rat-Race coupler based on coupling-enhanced structure, and the principle is introduced in detail. Based on the existing coupling scheme of the filtering Rat-Race coupler, a coupling-enhanced structure has been introduced. This design method can significantly increase the relative bandwidth by utilizing a coupling topology network to design the filtering Rat-Race coupler. In order to verify the feasibility of the design method, a filtering Rat-Race coupler operating at 2 GHz was designed using microstrip technology. The designed filtering Rat-Race coupler replaces the coupling nodes with a $\lambda / 2$ stepped-impedance resonator (SIR). The simulation results indicate that the designed filtering Rat-Race coupler has an insertion loss of 3.31 dB at the center frequency, a return loss better than 22 dB, and an isolation better than 23 dB. The relative bandwidth reaches $20 \%$, while maintaining a compact size of approximately $0.25 \lambda \mathrm{~g} \times 0.25 \lambda \mathrm{~g}$.

articleTitle: Optimization of Bayesian Inference Algorithm in Multimodal Data Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper proposes an optimized Bayesian inference algorithm, which aims to improve fusion accuracy and computational efficiency by improving the model structure and introducing an adaptive weighting mechanism. Specifically, this paper optimizes the algorithm’s computational process by adjusting the structure of the Bayesian network, using methods such as variational inference and distributed computing, and reduces the computational burden in the data fusion process. In addition, this paper also proposes a new data uncertainty modeling strategy that can better handle the noise and missing value problems of different modal data. Through experimental verification in multiple scenarios such as smart home, medical diagnosis, and autonomous driving, the results show that the optimized algorithm performs significantly better than the traditional Bayesian inference method on multiple data sets. In experiment A, the fusion accuracy of the optimized algorithm is improved by 10%, and the computational time is reduced by 15%; in experiment B, the error rate is reduced by 12%, and the computational efficiency is improved by 18%. The experimental results show that the proposed optimization algorithm can effectively improve the accuracy and efficiency of multimodal data fusion, and has good scalability and real-time performance.

articleTitle: Ship Equipment Modeling Method Based on Neural Networks and Particle Swarm Optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To address the challenges in ship equipment control simulation and the complexity of building equipment mechanism models, a data-driven equipment modeling approach is proposed. This method aims to enhance model prediction accuracy and generalization capability through the construction of neural network models and optimization via Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO). First, a data-driven neural network model is developed using real ship operational data. Then, the connection weights of the neural network are optimized using PSO to reduce prediction errors and improve model performance. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves the prediction accuracy of critical ship equipment, reduces the Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and increases the Coefficient of Determination ($\mathrm{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$). The proposed neural network and PSO-based modeling approach offers a novel perspective and effective tools for the simulation and optimization of ship equipment.

articleTitle: Emergency Disposal Decision Generation Method for Flight Test Based on Knowledge Graph
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The purpose of this study is to propose a new emergency response decision support method for real-time monitoring in flight test. Based on semantic understanding and generation model, the system can effectively generate emergency handling strategies, verify and update handling processes, and intelligently distribute handling tasks. Firstly, by integrating semantic understanding and generation model with flight test monitoring and emergency response professional knowledge base, the dynamic generation module of disposal strategy can independently generate emergency response strategy and provide decision support. Then, the processing strategy verification and update module realizes the verification and update of the generation strategy by using the multi-dimensional quantifiable characteristics of Petri Net model to ensure the real-time and effectiveness of the strategy. Finally, the intelligent distribution module of emergency handling task uses the deep learning model based on BERT to identify named entities and extract relationships, and constructs a detailed knowledge graph of < handling task-belonging-topic>, and realizes the intelligent distribution of tasks through Neo4j graph database and Cypher query language. Through this comprehensive decision support method, this study provides an effective solution for safety-assisted decision making in the field of flight monitoring and emergency response, and opens up a new direction for the application of large language models in this field.

Author Keywords: flight test monitoring emergency response decision

articleTitle: Enhancing Heterogeneous Data Processing Efficiency in 5G Networks using Transfer Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The heterogeneous nature of data formats, sources and network requirements represents a significant challenge for the heterogeneous data processing that is a hallmark of the rapidly developing 5G network. The efficient processing of this data is of critical importance in maintaining low latency and high-quality real-time services. This study proposes the implementation of a transfer learning-based model with the objective of enhancing the processing efficiency of heterogeneous data in 5G networks. The model transfers the learned features to a new diverse dataset through pre-training on similar data types, thereby optimising the data processing process and avoiding the necessity for a large number of retrainings. The model comprises two key components: adaptive feature mapping and a flexible architecture that enables adaptation to new data features while minimising computational costs. The results of the experimental analysis demonstrate that the model has a considerable impact on reducing processing time and enhancing data throughput.

articleTitle: Blade Segmentation Based on Improved FCN Network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To address the issues of limited dataset size and inaccurate fault region localization, this paper proposes an improved fully convolutional neural network (CBAM-FCN8s) based on the attention mechanism convolutional block embedding. This method introduces the CBAM module into the classic FCN8s network, enhancing attention to key regions and features through the attention mechanism, thereby improving fault segmentation and localization accuracy. To tackle the issue of insufficient datasets, this paper employs data augmentation techniques, such as random cropping, flipping, and scaling, to enhance the model’s generalization ability. For wind turbine blade faults in complex scenarios, combining the pixel-level segmentation capability of FCN with the CBAM module allows for precise segmentation of the fault area and enhances attention to key regions. Experimental results show that the CBAM-FCN8s network improves mean pixel accuracy and segmentation accuracy by 2.52% to 11.63% and 2.06% to 5.60%, respectively, compared to the traditional FCN32s, FCN16s, and FCN8s, significantly improving the accuracy and localization precision of fault segmentation.

articleTitle: A Smoke and Fire Detection Model Based on Improved YOLO11
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Smoke and fire detection plays a critical role in environmental monitoring and disaster prevention. However, due to the diverse and complex manifestations of smoke and fire, existing deep learning-based detection methods often suffer from insufficient feature extraction capabilities and high false positive rates. To address these issues, we propose a novel smoke and fire detection method called RSW-YOLO, which is based on the improved YOLOv11n. First, the structural reparameterization technology is introduced in the C3k2 module (RepC3k2), which enhances the model’s feature extraction capability and detection accuracy while maintaining efficient inference. Second, the SEGE attention is employed to suppress irrelevant background information and enhance key feature representations, effectively mitigating interference from false targets. Finally, applying the WIoUv3 loss function reduces the impact of adverse gradients caused by low-quality instances in the dataset. In evaluations on the D-Fire dataset, RSW-YOLO achieves $\mathbf{8 0. 8 \%}, 73.1 \%$, and 79.8% on P, R, and mAP@50, significantly outperforming existing methods. This research provides a new technical paradigm for smoke and fire detection in complex scenarios.

articleTitle: Research on Mine Fire Monitoring System Based on Information Fusion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Analyzed the fire monitoring data content and data characteristics of the mine fire related monitoring system, established a metadata standard and metadata model for mine fires, and collected, integrated, and visualized the data of subsystems related to mine fire monitoring and fire prevention, such as fiber optic temperature measurement, bundle tube monitoring, goaf nitrogen injection, goaf yellow mud grouting, goaf fly ash grouting, working face inhibitor fire extinguishing, and chamber jet fire extinguishing. The goal of continuous monitoring of mine fires was achieved, and emergency linkage response strategies for different areas of mine fires were formulated. Finally, the functionality of the entire system was designed and verified. The deep integration of data collection and governance technology with modern mine fire prevention and control can solve the problems of scattered mine fire data, difficult data interaction, low data utilization, and difficult integration and collaboration, laying a solid foundation for achieving comprehensive intelligent perception and accurate early warning of coal mine fires.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Real-Time Calibration Method for Nonlinear ADC Links Based on Compensation Sequence Lookup Tables
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper introduces a real-time calibration method for analog-to-digital conversion (ADC) link nonlinearity using a compensation sequence lookup table (LUT), implemented on an FPGA. The approach includes offline extraction of nonlinear errors and FPGA-based real-time calibration. Offline extraction uses a sinusoidal code density histogram to derive the compensation sequence, while the FPGA calibration unit—comprising an input converter, storage unit, compensation calculator, and buffer output—applies real-time corrections to the digital signal. With a 12 -bit resolution, 200 M sampling rate, and $\mathbf{9 0 \%}$ FSR sinusoidal input, the calibrated ADC link achieved an SFDR of $\mathbf{7 8. 2} \mathbf{~ d B c}$ and a THD of $\mathbf{- 8 2. 3} \mathbf{~ d B c}$, improving performance by 8% and 14% respectively. Nonlinear error fluctuations were also reduced by $\mathbf{3 0 \%}$, significantly mitigating harmonic interference.

articleTitle: Temporal Convolutional Network-Based Model for Precision Time-Series Forecasting in Marine Fisheries
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Recent advancements in sensor technology have made it increasingly feasible to collect long-term, continuous data. However, challenges related to data completeness, timeliness, and quality remain prevalent, undermining the reliability of predictive models. This study proposes a time series prediction model tailored for marine fisheries, addressing these limitations by leveraging Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs). Specifically, the model incorporates a Temporal Convolutional Network (TCN), which excels at identifying intrinsic patterns and hierarchical structures within large-scale marine time-series data, thereby enhancing model interpretability. The TCN framework demonstrates robust performance in capturing temporal dependencies and uncovering latent patterns, providing a comprehensive approach to managing the complex dynamics of marine data. This research applies the TCN deep learning model to examine the intricate relationships and information flow among various water quality parameters, tackling issues such as sequence distribution shifts and overfitting. Additionally, an interactive learning strategy is introduced to optimize hidden layer configurations and activation functions, further enhancing the predictive accuracy of the model. The results indicate that the proposed approach significantly improves both the timeliness and accuracy of predictions, offering valuable support for intelligent management in marine fisheries.

Index Terms: Activation Function Of The Hidden Layer

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of a High-Speed PPM-SPAD System Based on Multi-Aperture Reception
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To address the challenges of severe signal attenuation and weak signal detection in satellite-to-ground optical communication, this paper proposes a pulse position modulation-single photon avalanche diode (PPM-SPAD) scheme based on a single-input multiple-output (SIMO) structure. In this scheme, multiple SPAD receivers are deployed at the receiver end to mitigate the impact of the inherent dead-time characteristics of SPADs on system performance through reception diversity. A theoretical analysis framework is established in this study, and expressions for the bit error rate (BER) of the SIMO PPM-SPAD system, considering the effects of dead time, are derived. The accuracy of the theoretical analysis is validated through simulations. The simulation results demonstrate that the SIMO structure can effectively exploit reception diversity to gain significant improvement in BER performance. This research provides a solid theoretical foundation and practical guidance for the design and optimization of satellite-to-ground optical communication systems, showcasing the great potential of the SIMO PPM-SPAD scheme in enhancing system transmission performance.

Author Keywords: pulse position modulation-single photon avalanche diode

articleTitle: Credit Default Prediction with Machine Learning: A Comparative Study and Interpretability Insights
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This study built an efficient credit default prediction framework based on the LightGBM model, aiming to improve the prediction performance and enhance the interpretability of the model. Through experiments on the public Home Credit Default Risk dataset, this paper comprehensively compared LightGBM with SVM, XGBoost, GBDT, and random forest models, and verified the superiority of LightGBM from multiple indicators such as accuracy, recall, and F1-score. The experimental results show that LightGBM performs best in processing complex high-dimensional data with its efficient feature selection and optimization capabilities. At the same time, combined with SHAP value analysis, it reveals the impact of features on model decisions, providing transparent and reliable decision support for credit risk assessment. This study not only provides an effective technical solution for financial institutions to improve risk management efficiency but also lays the foundation for the application of machine learning algorithms in the financial field. In the future, multimodal data and deep learning technology will be further integrated to build a more powerful prediction model.

articleTitle: Python to FPGA: Automatic Implementation of custom CNN Model on FPGA
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence neural network technology, the architecture of convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has been evolving towards greater complexity and deeper hierarchical structures. Compared with CPUs and GPUs, Field-Programmable Gate Array (FPGA) are widely used in the inference process of CNNs due to its stability and high efficiency. However, implementing the inference process of CNNs on FPGAs requires great effort and expertise. Therefore, we propose a fast CNN conversion tool that can automatically generate FPGA hardware for customized CNNs inference tasks. The conversion tool takes the Python algorithms of the forward path of the CNN as input and outputs the corresponding FPGA CNN hardware. The Python program used is based on the CNN program based on the Pytorch and TensorFlow frameworks. The tool extracts the key information of each layer in the input CNN model and stores the model structure information in the configuration file. A general-purpose RTL template library is designed for each layer of the CNNs, and by parsing the configuration file, we call different layer templates to generate the complete FPGA CNN hardware. In addition, the weight and bias data of the CNN model trained on the PC will also be automatically converted and stored in the configuration file. We validated the proposed method by automatically converting the LeNet- 5 model implemented in the Pytorch framework and achieved a through-put of 0.25 GOPS and a power-efficiency ratio of 1.08 GOPS/W on the Xilinx FPGA ZYNQ 7010.

articleTitle: Optimization of Container Cloud Elastic Scaling Integrating ARIMA Forecasting and HPA Response
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Load changes of cloud computing resources show more and more complex characteristics. Load forecasting is crucial for elastic scaling of cloud computing resources. Kubernetes is a mainstream container cloud platform. Its built-in HPA policy automatically adjusts the number of Pod replicas according to load changes to achieve elastic scaling, but it has the problems of single load metric and user response delay during peak periods. This paper proposes a container cloud elastic scaling optimization method based on load forecasting and response, which dynamically monitors and calculates the combined load of CPU and Memory in the Pod set, uses ARIMA model to complete the combined load forecasting value based on historical data, and HPA responsive algorithm to make up for the lack of forecasting. Experimental results show that compared with the HPA strategy, our method can execute the corresponding scaling operations in advance, and can effectively reduce the response delay time and improve the Qos quality.

articleTitle: Research on network security situation analysis based on wavelet transform and support vector machine
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a novel approach to analyzing network security by integrating wavelet transform and Support Vector Machine (SVM) techniques. With the increasing complexity of network environments and the prevalence of cyberattacks, traditional security analysis methods struggle to accurately model the nonlinear and dynamic nature of network traffic. The proposed method employs wavelet decomposition to extract multi-scale features from network traffic and utilizes SVM for robust pattern recognition and predictive modeling. Experimental results based on real-world network traffic demonstrate that the proposed model significantly improves prediction accuracy and reduces the rates of common attack types, such as Denial-of-Service (DoS) and unauthorized access attacks. Additionally, the model’s efficiency in training and adaptability to diverse attack patterns make it a promising solution for modern network security challenges.

articleTitle: Synthetic Aperture Radar Ship Detection Network Based on Multi-Scale Feature Enhancement
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The paper introduces a ship identification network with SAR imagery, termed Multi-scale Feature enhancement YOLOX (MF-YOLOX), specifically designed to tackle the challenge of poor accuracy in recognizing multi-scale targets under complex circumstances posed by existing algorithms. Within the feature extraction network, the EMA module is incorporated to efficiently encode global spatial information and establish both short-term and long-term dependencies. Furthermore, the CIoU loss function is employed to substitute the original IoU in the prediction network, aiming to mitigate the positional bias issue of the prediction frame and enhance the model’s precision in the field of target localization. Experimental outcomes based on the HRSID dataset demonstrate that our approach achieves an $\mathbf{F} 1$ score of 89%, an average accuracy mean Average Precision (mAP) of $\mathbf{9 1 \%}$, and a detection speed of 51 Frames Per Second (FPS). Our approach offers the highest detection accuracy and operating efficiency when compared to some advanced methods, providing technical support for precise ship detection in complex maritime conditions.

articleTitle: Active receiving serial communication debugging method based on LabVIEW
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper provides a debugging method of serial communication based on LabVIEW active receiving, which solves the problem of incomplete data acquisition and high system resource occupation in LabVIEW-based active receiving serial communication. The test results show that the method is simple, reliable and practical, which can ensure the integrity and accuracy of the collected data, reduce the occupation of processors and resources, and make the system run smoothly.

articleTitle: A High-Temperature, Low-Drift Instrumentation Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In industrial control, detection devices need to operate at temperatures several times higher than room temperature. High-temperature environments can lead to offset voltage, increased noise, and reduced closed-loop gain accuracy in integrated circuits. This paper presents the design of an instrumentation amplifier circuit with offset self-calibration. The circuit employs an improved constant $\mathbf{G m}$ biasing circuit for secondary compensation, enabling the instrumentation amplifier to exhibit low offset and low noise characteristics over a wide temperature range. Simulation results indicate that within the temperature range of $-55^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$ to $175^{\circ} \mathrm{C}$, the equivalent input offset voltage is less than 777.711 nV, the input bias current is less than 26.398 nA, the total supply current is 2.747 mA, the commonmode rejection ratio is greater than 129.492 dB, and the 1 kHz noise is $75.55 \mathbf{n V} / \sqrt{ } \mathbf{H z}$.

articleTitle: Research on the adjustment of reflective surface of “FAST” based on geometric transformation and genetic algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Aiming at the adjustment problem of the active reflecting surface of radio telescope (FAST), this paper adopts the method of combining geometric coordinate transformation and genetic algorithm. Firstly, in the case of the base position, the coordinates of the vertex of the ideal paraboloid under the base position are determined as $(0,0,-300.4)$ by constructing the transformation model of the ideal paraboloid in terms of polar coordinates and right angle coordinates. Then, for the case that the observed celestial body is in the general position ($\alpha=$ $36.795^{\circ}, \beta=78.169^{\circ}$), the spatial coordinate transformation formula is used to extend the model to the observation scene of multiple angles, and combined with the geometrical motion characteristics of the main cable node and the actuator, the amount of regulation of the main cable node is finally optimized by the genetic algorithm to ultimately achieve the adjustment of the active reflecting surface to make it fit more closely to the ideal paraboloid. The shape of the active reflective surface is finally adjusted by optimizing the adjustment amount of the main cable node through the genetic algorithm, so that the shape of the active reflective surface can be adjusted to fit the ideal paraboloid.

articleTitle: Research on Mobile Edge Computing Task Offloading Strategy with Dual-Layer UAV Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Aiming at the natural disaster scenarios where the base station is destroyed and the problem of insufficient computing power during UAV information collection, a double-layer UAV MEC system task offloading scheme is proposed. First, the B-UAV resource scheduling, offloading strategy and T-UAV mobility are jointly optimized to minimize the total system cost; second, the TD3-OPS algorithm is proposed by combining the TD3 algorithm, the state normalization process, the use of OU noise with simulated annealing idea, and the improvement of the preferred empirical replay mechanism; lastly, the simulation results show that the proposed algorithm converges faster compared to the baseline algorithm and can significantly reduce the total system cost.

articleTitle: The ℓ1-SVD Algorithm For Regularization Parameter Selection Basis On The BIC Criterion
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The $\ell_{1}$-SVD algorithm is a compressive sensing algorithm based on $\ell_{1}$-norm constraints, but it can suffer from problems such as false targets and difficulties in selecting regularization parameters. Therefore, this paper proposes a spherical harmonic domain source localization algorithm based on the weighted $\ell_{1}$-SVD algorithm, abbreviated W-SHD-L1SVD. In this work, based on the orthogonality of the signal and noise subspaces, we construct a weighted coefficient vector to apply weighting to the $\ell_{1}$-norm constraint model. Additionally, an improved BIC criterion is used to automatically determine the regularization parameter to address the issue of regularization parameter selection. Through this weighting process and automatic regularization selection, the proposed algorithm enhances the sparsity of the recovered coefficient matrix and effectively suppresses false peaks, thereby achieving accurate direction of arrival (DOA) estimation. The simulation results prove that W-SHD-L1SVD is effective.

articleTitle: OTFS Channel Estimator based on Embedded Pilot Sequence Similarity
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Traditional orthogonal time-frequency space (OTFS) channel estimation schemes place guard symbols around pilots to avoid interference from data symbols, thereby reducing spectrum efficiency (SE). To address this issue, this paper proposes an OTFS channel estimator based on the similarity of embedded pilot sequences (EPSS). Firstly, according to prior channel information, multiple pilots are sparsely embedded into an OTFS data frame, preventing mutual interference between pilots while fully utilizing the channel diversity gain, and the guard symbols of the pilots at the transmitter are revoked to improve SE. Secondly, at the receiver, a shift sequence with strong correlation to the embedded pilot sequence at the transmitter is designed. Through linear search, when the autocorrelation value of the shift sequence with the pilot sequence is greater than a threshold, the delay-Doppler taps of the channel can be estimated. Finally, an inverse gain matrix is designed to eliminate interference from data symbols to the pilots, thereby obtaining the channel gain. Through the design of an OTFS communication system, simulation results verify that the EPSS scheme significantly improves SE with a slight reduction in reliable communication performance.

articleTitle: Image Classification with Noisy and Unlabeled Samples
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In deep learning, data annotation poses a significant challenge, often resulting in datasets with missing labels or noisy annotations, both of which can severely degrade model performance. Addressing these issues is crucial for enhancing the accuracy and generalization of models. In this framework, multiple teacher models collaborate to produce robust pseudo-labels, while multiple student models utilize regularization terms to correct noisy annotations. Specifically, for labeled samples with noisy annotations, the teacher models generate more reliable labels from multiple perspectives by aggregating prediction results, thus alleviating the noise issue. For unlabeled samples, the label with the highest confidence from the teacher models’ outputs is selected as the pseudo-label. Experimental results demonstrate that this approach significantly improves model performance when handling datasets with both noisy and missing labels, highlighting its potential for deployment in practical applications.

articleTitle: Encoding Research Based on the Multiple Sneak Path Issues in Resistive Random Access Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Resistive Random Access Memory (ReRAM), as a non-volatile storage technology, has shown great potential in the storage field due to its high density and fast storage capabilities. However, its crossbar array structure gives rise to the issue of Sneak Path Interference (SPI) that significantly impacts data reliability. To address this challenge, this paper refines the general model of multiple sneak paths based on the number and combination types of these paths. Furthermore, an across-array coding scheme under multiple sneak paths is proposed. This scheme allocates low-density parity-check (LDPC) codewords to multiple memory arrays, reducing the correlation of channelcoded bits used for decoding, thereby achieving a diversity gain. Simulation results show that, under the multiple sneak path model, the cross-array coding scheme with LDPC coding can effectively improve the system’s error rate performance.

articleTitle: 3D Model Feature Optimization Technology Based on Area Weighting and Laplace Operator
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In the field of 3D model rendering, optimization issues are currently the main direction of research. Since new problems inevitably arise during the model simplification process, leading to a decline in model quality, it is necessary to consider the optimization of the model while simplifying. This paper introduces the average area of the first-order neighborhood triangles and the sharp feature degree as new constraint factors into the calculation of the folding cost on the basis of the conventional simplification algorithm Quadric Error Metrics (QEM), which enhances the ability to preserve feature areas. At the same time, in the optimization phase, the positions of model space vertices are adjusted and updated based on the Laplace operator, making the arrangement of the internal triangular mesh more in line with the Delaunay criterion and of higher quality. Through experimental verification, the improved algorithm in this paper, while ensuring the simplification of the model volume, also achieves the optimization of the model surface features, eliminating low-quality deformed triangular meshes

Author Keywords: Average Area of First-Order Neighborhood Triangles

articleTitle: Phishing Detection Model Integrating URL Characters and HTML Word Semantic Deep Features
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Deep learning methods, known for their powerful feature learning and classification capabilities, are widely used in phishing detection. To improve accuracy, this study proposes DPMLF (Deep Learning Phishing Detection Model with Multi-Level Features), which integrates URL character-level and HTML word-level semantic features. DPMLF utilizes character embeddings and parallel convolutional kernels to precisely extract local URL features. For HTML text, it employs word-level embeddings and stacked convolutional layers with dense connections to capture both local and long-range text information. The fully connected layer then fuses these features into a multi-level, fine-grained feature vector for classification. The results of experiments conducted on two public datasets with different scales show that DPMLF is accurate in phishing attack detection.

articleTitle: Research on Anti-Collision System of Urban Road
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In view of the complex environmental changes and the technical problems of single algorithm affecting unmanned driving safety in the anti-collision system of urban roads, the fusion of Faster R-CNN and SSD algorithms, and the multi-sensor technology method of lidar, high-definition camera and thermal sensor are used to achieve accurate pedestrian detection and ensure the information circulation around the vehicle. Matlab was used to carry out the simulation experiment of the urban road human-vehicle anti-collision system, and the results showed that the technical scheme of the urban road human-vehicle anti-collision system was feasible.

articleTitle: Privacy-Preserving Dynamic Resource Allocation for Vehicle-Pile-Grid Systems Based Homomorphic Encryption
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In vehicle-pile-grid collaborative operations, achieving data sharing and resource optimization is crucial for enhancing system efficiency and user experience. However, privacy protection and data security issues severely limit efficient collaboration among multiple stakeholders. This paper proposes a dynamic resource allocation strategy based on homomorphic encryption, enabling the integration of privacy protection and resource optimization through encrypted domain computations. By integrating a dynamic resource allocation model, the strategy considers multiple constraints such as user demands, grid load, and charging pile capacity, and builds a distributed computing framework for cross-stakeholder collaboration. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed method excels in resource allocation efficiency, security, and user satisfaction, providing a reliable technical foundation for collaborative operations in vehicle-pile-grid systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Classification of Very High-Resolution Remote Sensing Image Using Ensemble Specific Class Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The classification of very high-resolution remote sensing images is complex because of their intricate and detailed characteristics, necessitating exact classification techniques. The proposed method employs a class-specific ensemble (ESC) technique to classify very high-resolution (VHR) remote sensing images. The proposed method was compared to standard convolutional neural network (SC) classification methods, bagging with majority voting (BV) and weighted bagging (BW). The experiment was conducted 30 times to collect a comprehensive dataset to verify the proposed method’s reliability and precision. The ESC method was assessed using the paired t-test against the SC, BV, and BW methods under identical trial conditions. The results demonstrate that the ESC method outperforms the SC and BV methods at a significance level of 0.05 and the BW method at a significance level of $\mathbf{0. 1 0}$. The $\mathbf{t}$-test outcomes verified the presence of a substantial disparity in mean accuracy between the ESC and the other approaches. The results revealed the benefits of using the ESC method as an alternative, more practical method for classifying VHR images, resulting in enhanced performance in remote-sensing applications.

articleTitle: Research on Drone Network Security Issues under Quantum Attack Threats
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The rapid advancement of quantum computing poses significant challenges to traditional cryptographic methods. Algorithms such as Shor’s and Grover’s have substantially weakened the security of symmetric and asymmetric encryption, exposing critical vulnerabilities in drone networks, particularly in identity authentication and key exchange. This paper examines the impact of quantum computing on drone network security, introduces an enhanced Dolev-Yao model to address quantum threats, and explores security challenges in both centralized and distributed drone networks. Using the ProVerif tool, this study evaluates existing drone security protocols under quantum attack scenarios. The results reveal that current protocols are inadequate against quantum threats, underscoring the urgent need for post-quantum cryptographic solutions to ensure the security of drone networks.

articleTitle: Research on Hardware Configuration of Low Orbit Satellite Communication System
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This study evaluates how hardware configuration affects the performance of low-orbit satellite communication systems, focusing on improving efficiency and reliability through optimization. It assesses the configurations of satellite payloads, ground stations, and user terminals, finding that enhanced hardware setups significantly boost data speeds, reduce delays, and stabilize the system. Adjustments in high-power amplifiers and low-noise receivers were found to effectively improve signal quality and coverage. The study concludes that systematic hardware optimization not only boosts system performance but also cuts costs and increases commercial viability.

articleTitle: A Combination of Multilevel Green’s Function Interpolation Method with Multilevel Fast Multipole Algorithm for Efficient Simulation of Scattering of Dielectric and Conductive Objects
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In this paper, a combination of multilevel Green’s function interpolation method (MLGFIM) with multilevel fast multipole algorithm (MLFMA) for solving the electromagnetic radiation and scattering problems from dielectric and conductive objects is proposed. The combination of MLGFIM and MLFMA was initially proposed by Ming Chen et al. [1] and it exclusively employs electric field integral equation (EFIE), which limits its application to PEC (Perfect Electric Conductor) scenarios only. This paper expands the scope by integrating Poggio-Miller-Chang-Harrington-Wu-Tsai (PMCHWT) equations in integral formulation with MLFMA-MLGFIM to solve homogeneous dielectric and metallic problems. In conventional MLFMA, the length of the minimum box needs to exceed a specific threshold, usually $0.2 \lambda$, leading to an excessive number of unknowns within lowest boxes, particularly when problem involves refined elements. This, in turn, increases the memory demands for storing the nearfield impedance matrix of the MLFMA. The MLGFIM is utilized here to compute near-field part of the MLFMA, effectively reducing the number of unknowns per box, irrespective of its size. Additionally, QR factorization is implemented to compress the Green’s function with low rank for accelerating the far-field matrix calculation process in MLGFIM, thereby expediting the matrix-vector multiplications (MVM) for the MLFMA-MLGFIM. The numerical examples provided in this paper illustrate the precision and computational effectiveness of the method. In the numerical simulations of a fine structured metal dielectric composite, the proposed method exhibits a notable near-field memory storage reduction by the factor of 15.5 without compromising the accuracy and maintaining the same calculation time for each MVM.

articleTitle: Deep Contrastive Clustering for Protocol Analysis in 5G Network Engineering
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of 5G networks in satellite communication and vehicular communication systems, the complexity of communication and signaling interactions has significantly increased. Traditional protocol analysis methods primarily focus on high-level structured data, often neglecting the low-level binary data critical for understanding 5G-specific protocols. This paper proposes a novel approach that employs a deep contrastive clustering framework to analyze and classify unknown protocols in 5G communication networks. The proposed method leverages depthwise separable convolutions for feature extraction, transforming binary protocol data into structured feature representations while significantly reducing computational overhead. Additionally, by integrating contrastive learning into the clustering process, the framework enhances the discrimination of protocol embeddings through a positive-negative sample feedback mechanism, ensuring more accurate clustering results. Additionally, this paper collected and analyzed a comprehensive dataset of 5 G protocols, which includes wireless access layer protocols and core network communication protocols.

articleTitle: Integrated Drive Board Detection System Based on STM32
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To address the low detection efficiency, difficulty in setting up the detection environment, and complexity of the detection process for LAMOST fiber positioning robot drive boards, an integrated drive board detection system based on STM32 has been designed. The system uses a RL circuit to simulate the working environment of the drive board, collects the drive signals using a current sampling module, and employs a programmable touch screen for human-machine interaction.
