However, the unique structure of emails and the complexity of publishing strategies mean that current deep learning-based phishing email detection studies still require further performance enhancement. To effectively detect phishing emails, this paper proposes TFW-CNBL (Term Frequency and Word2Vec-CNN and BiLSTM), a deep detection model for phishing emails based on the fusion of term frequency and contextual semantic multi-features. The TFW-CNBL model generates a hybrid feature vector that comprehensively understands the characteristics of phishing emails by integrating term frequency and contextual information. The model combines a convolutional neural network (CNN) with an attention mechanism and a bidirectional long short-term memory network (BiLSTM), creating an underlying architecture capable of rapid text classification. The paper utilized a publicly available dataset from Kaggle containing 18,650 samples to train and test the TFW-CNBL model. Experimental results indicate that the TFW-CNBL model can effectively detect phishing emails, achieving an average accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score of $0.984,0.986,0.989$, and 0.987, respectively.

articleTitle: A Deep Learning-based Model for Anomaly Data Detection in Cloud Failure Scenarios
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The rapid development of cloud platform makes the traffic data show exponential growth. In order to ensure the stable operation of the business required by users, it is necessary to quickly detect the anomalous data in cloud platform failure scenarios. Considering the seriousness of the current network security situation as well as the problems of data clutter, data imbalance and incomplete feature learning of traditional network anomaly detection models, this paper proposes a deep learning data anomaly detection model based on CNN-BiLSTM-Attention and introduces the ADASYN algorithm to balance the number of samples. Experiments show that the model achieves 97% accuracy in Yahoo dataset and can effectively detect data anomalies in cloud platform.

articleTitle: MIN-DAS: The Digital Asset System Based on MIN Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose an innovative digital asset system based on the MIN (MIN-DAS), which integrates PPoV consortium blockchain technology along with NFT identifiers, achieving the rights confirmation, decentralization, and high security for digital asset trading. We first deployed the MIN-DAS within the high-security MIN network and designed a built-in MIN-VPN security tunnel, enabling end-to-end communication encryption, thereby significantly bolstering transaction security. Subsequently, we adopted the PPoV consortium blockchain as the core processing engine, greatly increasing the speed of transaction processing to accommodate large-scale transaction demands. Moreover, MIN-DAS supports stablecoin transactions, effectively mitigating risks stemming from cryptocurrency market fluctuations. MIN-DAS provides a secure and efficient solution for digital asset trading. Our experimental findings reveal that, compared to existing traditional digital asset platforms, MIN-DAS demonstrates significant superiority in both performance and security.

articleTitle: An Interference Signal Recognition Method Based on Feature Extraction and YOLOv8 in Low INR
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To enhance the recognition capability of wireless communication interference signals, this paper proposes an interference signal recognition method based on feature extraction and YOLOv8. First, mathematical models of 11 common types of interference signals are simulated. Then, a feature extraction method based on projection transformation is introduced to construct 2D image datasets of interference signals, generated by bispectrum transform (BT), Hilbert-Huang transform (HHT), and short-time Fourier transform (STFT) respectively. Finally, the YOLOv8 classification network is used for interference signal recognition. Experimental results show that the average recognition accuracy of STFT features is consistently higher than that of other features. Moreover, the proposed method based on STFT features and YOLOv8 attains a recognition rate of 100% when the interference-to-noise ratio (INR) exceeds 4 dB, outperforming other principal methods.

articleTitle: A Rule-Driven Approach for Safety-Violation Search in Autonomous Driving Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Autonomous driving systems (ADS) and robotic vehicles (RVs) have made significant advancements, yet safety and security challenges remain. Current approaches predominantly focus on external attacks and software vulnerabilities, while often neglecting critical safety concerns associated with the Safety of the Intended Functionality (SOTIF), which addresses faulty implementations and user misuse. This paper introduces RDA, a rule-driven fuzzing framework designed to uncover unexpected behaviors in ADS through the analysis of safety rules. RDA extracts these rules from vehicle manuals and translates them into Linear Temporal Logic (LTL) formulas for validation. The fuzzing engine mutates inputs based on these rules, using distance metrics to evaluate compliance with safety protocols. We validate RDA on ArduPilot, a widely-used open-source platform, and successfully identify misbehaviors linked to 28 extracted rules. This work uncovers previously unknown safety violations, contributing to the safety and reliability of ADS.

articleTitle: Function as a Service for Edge Computing: Challenges and Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The widespread adoption of mobile devices and large-scale deployment of edge IoT devices have ushered humanity into an era of intelligent interconnectivity. Currently, the computing architecture dominated by cloud data centers is increasingly struggling to meet the growing demand for edge computing services. As a result, the concept of edge computing has been proposed and widely studied in recent years. Meanwhile, Function as a Service (FaaS) is driving cloud computing service technologies toward more flexible and fine-grained models. By effectively combining edge computing with FaaS, it is possible to leverage the strengths of each, addressing the unique requirements of edge-intelligent applications, such as low latency, dependency on edge data, privacy protection, low-frequency requests, and traffic bursts. However, as research on this model is still in its early stages, this paper summarizes the latest research and analyzes the challenges and potential solutions faced by this architectural model. Specifically, the following tasks are carried out: 1) A brief review of the development status of edge computing and FaaS; 2) A discussion of the issues arising from introducing FaaS in the edge computing environment, identifying six key challenges for the future; 3) Proposing four possible solutions for FaaS applications in edge computing environments, based on the analysis of existing research and related work; 4) Listing four major open-source serverless frameworks and five leading edge serverless platform providers, along with their main features.

articleTitle: Comparative analysis of traffic flow prediction based on XGBoost before and after optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Due to the imbalance between the supply side and the demand side, the continuous urbanization process has challenged road traffic transportation, and improving the efficiency of road traffic transportation has become one of the challenges facing traffic engineering in the new era, in which the improvement of algorithmic prediction ability in machine learning has become one of the core of the solution. This study analyzes the accuracy and time benefit of XGBoost algorithm SSA optimization before and after two traditional deep learning in deep learning class models and simulates the fitting of time series feature data in the same space. From the simulation results, the models built in this study before and after optimization and the two traditional deep learning are within the error tolerance, and we believe that the prediction results using the optimized SSA-XGBoost are better for our dataset.

articleTitle: Federated Learning for Resource Allocation in Maritime IoT Networks with Compressed Sensing
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Maritime transportation and shipping are vital components of global economic development.In order to enhance shipping efficiency and ensure safety, a distributed machine learning architecture can be utilized to achieve it. Due to concerns about data privacy, many shipping data are not shared. Federated learning $(\mathbf{F L})$, as a form of distributed machine learning, offers the advantage of preserving privacy. The problem of communication efficiency and resource joint optimization in FL over communication networks has been studied, and proposed a communication resource allocation algorithm with compressed sensing. Through experiments, we found that compared to the basic FL method with uniform resource allocation, the proposed RACS algorithm significantly improves the communication efficiency of wireless IoT network FL, as well as the learning performance in terms of training loss and testing accuracy.

articleTitle: Merging and cooperative caching based HDFS small files access performance optimization
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a performance optimization method for accessing small files in HDFS based on merging an d co-caching strategies to address the memory overhead problem caused by massive small files in Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS). First, the small files stored in HDFS are merged into multiple large files based on the descending first adaptation algorithm, thus saving the memory space occupied by the management node (NameNode). Second, in order to improve the read speed of s mall files, this paper proposes a two-level collaborative caching strategy, i.e., the server-side caching adopts the improved GDSF (G reedy Dual Size Frequency) strategy for small files, and the client -side adopts the ARC (Adaptive Replacement Cache) caching strategy for the small file indexes. The Experiments show that compared with genetic algorithm and particle swarm algorithm, the number of large files generated by merging small files using descending first adaptation algorithm is reduced by 26 and 60 on average. Compared with the original GDSF strategy, the co-caching strategy proposed in this paper improves the server-side cache hit rate by 8.2% on average. Compared with the FIFO and LRU cache re placement strategies, the client-side cache hit ratio is improved by 2.7% and 8.9%, respectively.

articleTitle: Optimization Strategies for Heliostat Field Design Based on Enhanced Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: As a novel clean energy technology with low carbon emissions, Concentrated Solar Power (CSP) with a power tower is of paramount importance to China’s sustainable development strategy. This paper addresses the optimization of heliostat fields in tower solar thermal power generation, a novel low-carbon and environment-friendly clean energy technology pivotal to China’s sustainable development strategy. The technical challenge of maximizing power generation efficiency through optimal heliostat field design is tackled by constructing a calculation model for the optical efficiency of heliostats. Through the application of stereographic projection geometry, the research delineates the intricate spatial interplay between the heliostat plane, the receiver tower and the sun, enabling refined model development. Utilizing an adaptive genetic algorithm enhanced by an elitist strategy, this paper successfully identifies the optimal adjustment strategies for various decision variables to maximize optical efficiency. This study culminates in achieving an annual average optical efficiency of 0.5784. This finding not only contributes to the efficiency optimization of solar thermal power generation but also offers a methodological advancement in the design and analysis of heliostat fields.

articleTitle: An Efficient and Flexible Black-Box Watermarking Framework for Large Language Models
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: To prevent misuse of text generated by large language models (LLMs), watermarking technology offers a straightforward and effective means of verification. Existing approaches, however, suffer from several limitations, including a high dependency on the underlying logic of LLMs, inadequate performance against sophisticated watermarking attacks, and poor stealth, making them less suitable for complex and dynamic real-world applications. To address these challenges, we propose an efficient and flexible black-box watermarking framework for large language models. This framework enhances robustness and stealth by embedding watermarks in key areas of the text through the identification and sampling of high-entropy words. Furthermore, we introduce an encryption-based encoding algorithm that allows users to verify watermarks with their personal keys, supporting the customization of watermarking algorithms. Comparative experiments on four datasets with five baseline methods demonstrate that the proposed method excels in accuracy while significantly improving robustness and concealability with minimal semantic changes.

articleTitle: Research on intelligent identification method of power grid wiring diagram based on deep convolution neural network
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The continuous evolution of smart grid technology has promoted the intelligent level of power dispatching automation systems to meet more stringent requirements and challenges. In the context of the growing demand for unified grid standards in power systems, there is an increasing importance in the collaborative integration and sharing of models, data, and graphs. This paper proposes a set of intelligent identification schemes for power grid graphics, combining convolutional neural network and OCR technology with CAD and PDF graphics files commonly used in power grids. The proposed solution is capable of accurately identifying information such as standard components, topology associations, and device labels in power grid graphs, and automatically converting this information into standard CIM/G file format. Furthermore, by introducing natural language processing technology, this paper effectively establishes a close relationship between graphic elements in CIM/G files and power grid model data, and achieves accurate recognition of graphic elements in power grid wiring diagrams, accurate extraction of character information, and comprehensive analysis of topology structure. The implementation of these technological innovations has established a solid foundation for advanced functions, such as automated management and rapid response to failures of the smart grid. The model association method employs image recognition to construct a power grid pattern recognition platform that assists dispatch centre management. The platform has been shown to refine graphics, integrate AI efficiency, provide a user-friendly interface, reduce labour requirements, ensure information accuracy and stabilise the operation of smart grids. Through the specific application in the engineering field, it is verified that this method improves the efficiency of model correlation, reduces the work of manual maintenance, and improves maintenance efficiency.

articleTitle: Power Allocation Strategy for Communication and Navigation Based on Multi-Beam LEO Satellite
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: This paper proposes a joint power allocation method for an integrated communication and positioning system in Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites, utilizing an innovative strategy based on spectral clustering and an improved genetic algorithm. Compared to traditional methods, the proposed approach first employs spectral clustering to group users, reducing intra-group interference and simplifying the power allocation problem. Then, an improved genetic algorithm is used to optimize the power allocation for positioning users, ensuring the Quality of Service (QoS) for communication users while maximizing positioning accuracy. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method significantly improves resource utilization efficiency in a multi-beam LEO satellite system, increasing the average positioning accuracy by 13% compared to traditional average power allocation methods.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Video Caching and Updating in Mobile Edge Computing Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Using mobile edge computing (MEC) servers to cache and update video resources can not only save network bandwidth and computing resources, but also adjust the bit rate of video playback according to real-time network conditions, providing users with ideal video quality of experience ($\mathbf{Q o E}$). In this work, we propose a novel video caching and updating optimization scheme, which enables the MEC server to provide video caching and updating services for users. To achieve this, we design a video caching and update optimization algorithm based on deep reinforcement learning adaptive bitrate selection, which can perceive environmental state information and determine its own caching strategy based on environmental feedback. We perform simulations and show that our algorithm can significantly reduce bandwidth and computing resources in the edge network and better improve video quality of service when compared with several existing algorithm.

articleTitle: ECPO: An enhanced Crested Porcupine Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The newly published Crested Porcupine Optimizer in 2024: The A new nature inspired metaheuristic algorithm has some problems that need further modification. The CPO algorithm is divided into four stages. The defense strategies in the first and second stages (visual and sound means) are shown in the global search stage, and the defense strategies in the third and fourth stages (odor and body attacks) are shown in the local optimization stage. Crested Porcupine Optimizer: The A new nature-inspired metaheuristic algorithm still belongs to the type of meta-heuristic algorithm, so it can not escape the problem of balancing the global search ability and the fast and accurate convergence of the local optimization while avoiding the local optima. In the second stage, the problem of excessive randomness appears, which will reduce the global search ability. The local convergence ability in the chapter third stage needs to get the corresponding good sum improvement, and the result accuracy of the local rapid convergence in the fourth stage can be further improved. However, after the verification of the test data, it is necessary to adopt a new improvement idea to improve the accuracy of the algorithm, rather than simply modifying a certain step. In the initialization stage, this paper adopts the algorithm of Tent-Logistic-Cosine chaotic mapping to handle the problem of population initialization, deleted the cyclic population reduction technology, and introduces a new opposition-based learning strategy and a new dynamic updating mechanism (parameter dynamic updating strategy, sine-cosine composite perturbation factor, Tent-chios and Cauchy mutation), and changed the idea of dynamic adaptive regulation and preliminary screening. But the four stages of CPO defense remain unchanged. Finally, a classical Levy cuckoo random walk model is added to solve the problem of local optimization, with the aim to jump out of the local optimum.

Author Keywords: jump out of the local optimum

articleTitle: Lightweight Large Receptive Field Network via Wavelet Convolution for Nighttime Flare Removal
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The task of nighttime flare removal aims to restore images damaged by flares, making it a new and valuable image restoration task with significant practical applications. During the flare restoration process, flares can be divided into large-area smooth streaks and high-contrast glare and shimmer types. Different types of flares occupy a large portion of the image and severely distort the background details, this requires the network to have a sufficiently large receptive field to handle large flares and the ability to recover fine local details. While some progress has been made in the field of nighttime flare removal, there is still a challenge in balancing receptive field size, parameter count, and local detail recovery in different approaches based on transformers and convolutions. To address this, we propose a nighttime flare removal network based on wavelet convolution (WCNFRN). To achieve a lightweight network with a large receptive field, we introduce a Wavelet Convolution Attention Module (WCAM) in the network. This module improves flare removal performance by combining a symmetric network structure, wavelet convolution groups, and a hybrid attention mechanism.

articleTitle: Detecting Adversarial Fake Tasks in Mobile Crowd sensing Platforms
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: The presence of fake tasks in mobile crowd sensing severely affects the normal operation of the platform. Due to the rapid development of deep learning, “Adversarial Fake Tasks” now have a greater destructive impact than traditional fake tasks. Traditional fake tasks are generated based on experience, while adversarial fake tasks are created using deep learning techniques to mimic real tasks, making them difficult to be detected. This paper proposes a “Spatial attention mechanism guided by distance” based on the multi-head self-attention mechanism to counter the threat of adversarial fake tasks in mobile crowdsensing platforms. This module captures the distance correlation between features of generated fake tasks and designs a detection model called Self Distance-Attention Convolution Crowdsensing Network (SDACC). Using SDACC as a detector, the detection steps based on the adversarial training defense strategy are as follows: firstly, utilize the generation model-SeqGAN to learn the distribution of real tasks and generate adversarial fake tasks; then train SDACC to detect adversarial fake tasks. Experiments on the MCS task datasets, the KDD Cup99 dataset, and the CICIDS-2017 dataset demonstrate that SDACC outperforms traditional detection algorithms in the MCS fake task detection domain, with average ACC, F1, and AUC reaching 0.9357,0.9332, and 0.9786 respectively.

articleTitle: Anti-UAV Net for Target Detection of Small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: With the widespread adoption of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), safety concerns have increasingly emerged. To mitigate these security issues, the accurate and rapid detection and identification of UAV targets—particularly smaller UAVs in complex backgrounds—has become an urgent challenge that requires immediate attention. Traditional object detection algorithms often struggle with accuracy and robustness due to various factors, including the small size of targets, complex backgrounds, and varying lighting conditions. To address these challenges, we propose a dual-modal small UAV detection network, termed Anti-UAV Net (AU-net), which utilizes adaptive fusion of infrared and visible images. Our model is built on the classic single-stage object detection framework YOLOv8n to satisfy real-time performance demands. We have designed an infrared-visible dual-modal feature extraction backbone and integrated the Simple Attention Module (SimAM) to facilitate adaptive weighted fusion of dual-modal feature maps. Additionally, we developed a small object detection layer specifically tailored for small UAV targets, enhancing the resolution of the final feature maps and improving the network’s effectiveness in detecting small UAVs. Experimental results show that the AU-net algorithm significantly improves the mean Average Precision (mAP) from 76.70% to 97.68% on the self-constructed Anti-UAV Dual-Modal Dataset (AU-dataset) compared to single-modal detection methods. The detection speed achieves 76 FPS, meeting the requirements for real-time processing.

articleTitle: obfFuzz: Empirical Study to Boost Fuzzing the Obfuscated Software
publicationTitle: 2024 4th International Conference on Communication Technology and Information Technology (ICCTIT)
abstract: Code obfuscation is a well-known method of protecting proprietary software against reverse engineering. Although obfuscation is beneficial, it alters the program’s control and data flow. Thus, systematic control and data flow alteration significantly affect the quality of the binaries, especially from the point of view of fuzzing testing. Although these modifications can introduce bugs in the program, there is still a lack of clear understanding of how implementing an obfuscation algorithm degrades the quality of fuzzing obfuscated software.This paper proposes obfFuzz, the first empirical study to reveal and understand the challenges behind the fuzzing of obfuscated software. Our study begins by fuzzing the unobfuscated binaries and comparing the results with obfuscated binaries. We chose the most popular fuzzing technique, AFL++. It is interesting because of its approach to combining mutation-based test case generation with code coverage metrics, which is the most affected component, by applying obfuscation transformation techniques. We have evaluated our tool on four real-world programs (pdfinfo, exif, tiffinfo, and md2roff). Our study revealed several findings: 1) Control flow obfuscation makes the code more complex, significantly decreasing the percentage of code coverage by $\mathbf{6 0 \%}$ compared to the original code. 2) Due to data flow obfuscation, we have inefficient mutations during fuzzing, so it takes $\mathbf{7 0 \%}$ more time to expose crashes than in the unobfuscated code with the same constraints. 3) Applying obfuscation techniques increases the program code size and decreases execution speed, giving us inefficient fuzzing results for the obfuscated binary. 4) Our observation shows that fuzzing an obfuscated binary is inefficient. Obfuscation transformations add more complexity, degrading the resultant binary and introducing buggy code.
